speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On the first area, artificial trans fat is harmful to health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: According to WHO, artificial trans fat increases the risk of heart disease and has no known health benefits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: WHO has called for countries to remove artificial trans fat from the food supply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Currently, our law requires food manufacturers to declare and limit the amount of trans fat in cooking oil and fats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: PHO is a major source of artificial trans fat in these foods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Banning PHO will not have an adverse effect on Singaporeans' food options and cost.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MOH has consulted the local food industry which is generally supportive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The US, Canada and Thailand have also banned PHO.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The industry will be given time to make adjustments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, turning to the second area: reducing smoking rates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: One in six smokers tell us that they are thinking about quitting, but only three in 100 smokers actually take action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We target to get more smokers to go beyond thinking about quitting to actually taking active steps to quit smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Successful cessation rates range from 10% for telephone-based interventions to 20% for programmes that combine intensive counselling and pharmacotherapy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: That is why it is called an addiction, but it is not impossible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Iskandar shared with me about how he successfully quit smoking, and he also helped his father to quit a 30-year smoking habit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Iskandar started smoking when he was 14.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: After smoking for about eight years, he started his quit journey last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: He wanted to save money for travel and improve himself.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Iskandar shared his quit journey with his father, Mr Muhamed Ibrahim, a smoker of 30 years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The son motivated the father and his father had also quit smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Iskandar is now working on his brother, Mr Noor Muhamed, to cut back on smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are learning points from Mr Iskandar's story.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Studies show that self-motivation and important milestones, such as the arrival of a new baby, or discovering a serious disease, are critical turning points.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And third, it is never too late to quit smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will be speaking with more smokers this year to see how we can help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Details will be shared in HealthySG Task Force's recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are some who have suggested e-cigarettes as smoking cessation aids.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Members are aware that we disallowed the importation, sale, distribution, purchase, possession and use of e-cigarettes since February 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Cessation products and programmes must first be effective and evidence-based.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The current evidence for e-cigarettes as a smoking cessation aid is mixed, and we are monitoring studies that have been conducted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: One concern we have is a "substitution effect".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Some smokers substitute cigarettes with e-cigarettes instead of quitting or, worse, they use both.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It is more like swapping one nicotine/tobacco addiction in one guise for another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Various studies have shown that e-cigarette users are more likely to become cigarette smokers compared to non-users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The experience with e-cigarettes in the US and Hong Kong are instructive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The US Surgeon-General has called the alarming increase in new cigarette use an epidemic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Hong Kong reported a rise in Primary 2 to Primary 4 students trying e-cigarettes in the last two years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are open to allowing a specific product to be registered and regulated under the Health Products Act as a therapeutic product for smoking cessation, but there must be good evidence and it must be effective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about help for younger smokers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But this means that there are still 12,000 underaged smokers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are focused not only on preventing initiation, but also helping younger smokers quit, and this is our strategy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: HSA has stepped up ground surveillance and enforcement activities among tobacco retailers to reduce youth access to tobacco.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Youth smokers are referred to counsellors, Quitline or Student Health Advisors at 50 secondary schools or ITE colleges and polytechnics for cessation counselling.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In 2017, 3,000 youths were counselled and 43% managed to reduce smoking, and about 10% quit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In June 2018, we launched "Better Things to Do", a campaign for youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We hope to encourage youths to tap on their network to promote a tobacco-free lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And in January this year, we focused on harmful, emerging products, e-cigarettes in particular, which contain nicotine and benzene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, turning to the third area of my speech, strengthening our health ecosystem, I have three points to make.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: First, growing our healthcare professionals and traditional Chinese medicine practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And third, the progress on the War on Diabetes and the HealthSG Task Force.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On the first point, Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about ensuring sufficient numbers of allied health professionals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are also Graduate Entry Masters programmes in Speech Therapy, Clinical Psychology and Audiology at NUS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For example, for the growing need of dietitians in Singapore, SIT launched the first local four-year Dietetics and Nutrition degree programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The first cohort will begin the programme in September 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Earlier this year, we introduced an accelerated the PCP for Physiotherapists as an additional pathway for those keen to join the healthcare sector as Physiotherapists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This programme allows mid-career locals with a degree in science-related fields to complete physiotherapy training in less than three years, compared to four.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Skills Framework for Healthcare is a common reference for skills and competencies for different stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MOH will work closely with the respective professions to identify training needs and build a future-ready healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Turning to TCM practitioners, to raise professional standards of TCM practitioners, Continuing Professional Education (CPE) is compulsory when renewing practising certificates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To defray CPE costs, TCM practitioners can apply for the TCM Development Grant, launched in 2018, at a cap of $200 per year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: TCM practitioners can use their SkillsFuture Credit to attend eligible TCM-related courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And we will continue to work closely with the TCM associations to support TCM practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will make health screening and follow-up more convenient.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will update our guidelines to recommend the use of glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) and the non-fasting lipid tests as alternative screening tests for diabetes and high blood cholesterol respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This has been endorsed by international and local medical professional bodies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A local clinic working group found that the HbA1c, if used correctly, was just as capable as the current test in detecting diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The group also recommended the use of non-fasting lipid profiles for screening high cholesterol based on international guidelines and studies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The non-fasting tests give Singaporeans a wider range of screening options to choose from.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will be helpful for seniors who are more prone to episodes of low blood sugar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We hope to increase screening uptake with this added convenience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporeans with eye conditions can now receive care closer to their homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We piloted community eye clinics with Singapore National Eye Centre, Tan Tock Seng Hospital and National University Hospital.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: At the Community Eye Clinics (CECs), patients can have their eyes checked and managed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are four CECs at Punggol Polyclinic, Keat Hong Family Medicine Clinic, Hougang Polyclinic and the Health Promotion Board at Outram.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Later this year, there will be two more CECs at Pioneer and Geylang Polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Dr Lily Neo asked about promoting healthy lifestyles to prevent chronic diseases and supporting Singaporeans to reduce sugar intake.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked for updates on the War on Diabetes and Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked for updates on the HealthySG Taskforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As of December 2018, more than 1,200 food and beverage (F&B) operators, hawker centres and coffee shops, with 8,900 touchpoints island-wide, have joined the Healthy Dining Programme (HDP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have more drink partners with about 200 outlets, as well as drink stalls in hawker centres and coffee shops with the "H", with the HDP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: HPB’s Eat Drink Shop Healthy Campaign nudges Singaporeans to earn points when choosing healthier options during grocery shopping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We extended the Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme to include sugar-sweetened beverages, desserts and sauces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We partnered five dessert suppliers, three beverage suppliers and one sauce supplier, and there are now healthier options available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The National Steps Challenge Season 3 helped eight in 10 participants who were previously inactive clock more than 150 minutes of physical activity a week.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are encouraging higher-intensity physical activity, hence, better fitness, and 740,000 participants in Season 4 of the National Steps Challenge were provided with a new step-tracker that can measure heart rate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There were also many exercise programmes in the community, but there is more to do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The HealthySG Taskforce, which I chair, seeks to integrate, coordinate, scale up health promotion efforts across our social and infrastructure agencies and communities, and especially the under-reached and disadvantaged groups, such as the lower-income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Public consultations will start in end March to early May, and we are targeting to release recommendations in early second half of the year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad asked about how health promotion efforts have reached our Malay and Indian communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, in Malay, please.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   Our effort to develop a healthy Malay community focuses on three aspects: first, by watching what we eat and drink; second, be physically active; and third, undergo health screenings and seek early treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Many initiatives introduced this year have refreshed the three thrusts mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Halal Healthier Choice dishes now include chicken porridge, Penang asam laksa and mee bakso.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Crowd favourites like briyani, nasi padang, chicken rice, rendang and many other kinds of dishes can also be modified into healthier versions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The dishes taste the same and the flavour is not compromised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In January this year, we offered get-fit courses to those getting married at the Wedding Fair.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: One hundred and forty couples who are tying the knot participated in this pilot programme so that, on their big day, they will be lighter, slimmer and, more importantly, healthier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our "Kita dah cukup manis!" (We are sweet enough!) and "Korang OK?" (Are You OK?) campaigns, especially during the fasting and Hari Raya period, advise us to consume less sugar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In November 2018, I launched the “Korang OK?” exercise video for preschool children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To bend a bamboo, do it when it is still a bamboo shoot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This Malay proverb means to cultivate good values while they are still young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: From young, develop healthy habits, exercise, as these can be done easily and enjoyably.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Six dialogue sessions sharing nuggets of wisdom on health were organised with Berita Harian.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It is always best to get medical advice from the professionals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Therefore, during these dialogue sessions, the public were able to obtain health tips from the experts, like doctors from the Muslim Healthcare Professionals Association.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The "Korang OK?" social media site set up in June 2018 has more than 23,000 followers and the site is actively sharing healthy recipes and health tips.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I was concerned when I saw many of our seniors experiencing leg pains when I performed my Umrah, or minor pilgrimage, in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Together with HPB and Umrah travel agents, we launched the "Get Fit For Haj/Umrah" in November 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The six-week exercise programme organised in mosques and stadiums attracted 900 participants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I was informed that, through this programme, our pilgrims were able to move quicker when performing their tawaf, that is, the haj ritual that involves walking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: After the Umrah season, there are also exercise programmes like the "Gerak Gelak" walking event organised by the Malay Activity Executive Committee from the community clubs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Four "Gerak Gelak" sessions were organised since 2018 by the Tampines, Marine Parade and Sembawang Group Representation Constituencies, as well as in Jurong last week, with a total of 2,200 participants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Taking care of health is also encouraged in Islam.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Let us take care of our health and our families together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In English): Let me now turn to the Indian community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I attended a dialogue with 20 Indian voluntary organisations to talk about community health matters and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are partnering various Indian groups, such as Sree Narayana Mission, the Central Sikh Temple, and Narpani Pearavai, which is the Indian Activity Executive Committees Council.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We partnered Suria, Vasantham and various Mediacorp artistes to run the Family Funival earlier this January.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Over 5,000 people bonded over zumba and various workouts.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I do not know about Members, but I feel very hungry after the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's speech!

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Chairman, my clarification is for the Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I hope she can address my cut on reviewing the medical evidence on preterm viability.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: According to local experts as well as based on our hospitals' experience, foetal viability below 24 weeks remains low.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Furthermore, morbidities, such as neuro-developmental disabilities, are very high among the premature babies who survived.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: International studies and professional bodies also largely support the low foetal viability below 24 gestational weeks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, essentially, the number of abortions below 24 but between 22 to 24 is already very low, and quite a large percentage is really due to medical reasons.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, what we have done, really, is also to work together with MSF to strengthen pre-abortion counselling and to raise awareness among these women with unplanned pregnancies of the options available to them, including adoptions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: MOH will continue to monitor and review this issue as new evidence emerges.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: One is concerning the Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE).

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I have been very supportive of it because it gives guidelines on what are the best practices.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: So, I was hoping that MOH could perhaps share with the House the achievements of ACE thus far.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Earlier this year, there were some concerns about inadequate payouts for certain patients.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I understand from previous replies that the MediShield Life Review Committee is looking at claims limits.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: But in the meanwhile, to give better assurance to Singaporeans, is there any mechanism by which we can appeal for higher payouts from MediShield Life in certain of these bills?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Dr Chia Shi-Lu for the supplementary question with regard to ACE.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: ACE was actually set up within MOH in August 2015 as a national health technology assessment agency against the backdrop of rising healthcare costs and the need to drive clinically effective and cost-effective healthcare.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Over the years, there has been a lot of good work done by ACE.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Just to name some of the achievements that ACE has done, which include producing technology guidances on drugs and medical technologies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition to that, ACE also produces Appropriate Care Guides (ACGs) which are targeted and concise as recommended care practices and pathways that promote appropriate prescribing behaviours.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As of 2 January this year, they have already produced nine ACGs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: ACE also conducts value-based pricing (VBP), in parallel with drug and medical technology evaluation.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is to ensure that the price of patented drugs or medical technologies recommended for subsidy commensurate with the drugs or medical technologies' value in Singapore's context.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, suffice to say, ACE has done a lot of good work and it has also achieved its objective of driving healthcare costs down.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Chairman, I will address Dr Chia Shi-Lu's second question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the MediShield claims limit is being reviewed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: First, in my earlier cut, I mentioned that patients now have access to information on bills and fee information on the MOH website.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: But there is no information on the website on the standard or quality of delivery, basically, qualitative information.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: So, would the Minister consider providing such information on the website, which I feel will be helpful?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: My second question: last year, MOH announced the formation of the Agency for Logistics and Procurement Services (ALPS) to pool together the supply chain functions and resources of the three health clusters.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I want to thank the Member for that suggestion.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is an important initiative that we have introduced.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Beyond that, the agency is also looking into how we can reorganise our distribution network, our logistics arrangement, our entire supply chain management so that we are able to optimise resources.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, if you can imagine that you store your pharmaceuticals in one warehouse and deliver them to another hospital, and you have another warehouse deliver to the other hospital, actually we can just have one warehouse to deliver to both hospitals.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, there is opportunity for us to optimise.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Lastly, having done some of these optimisations, we also want the agency to think out of the box to see whether they can have new innovative ways of managing the supply chain.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, if you allow your imagination to run wild a little bit, you can think about whether we can deliver medication to the patients rather than having to collect it from the pharmacy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, if you do a national kind of distribution network, that may be possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Today, many of us purchase through e-commerce and they deliver to your house quite regularly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But, of course, delivering medication is quite different from delivering your food items and sundries and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will have to study it very carefully.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But aggregating the supply chain and logistics function will allow us to think out of the box and develop new models of distribution which will, in the long term, benefit our patients.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Chairman, I do not recall hearing a response to my cut on the private ambulance service industry.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, may I have a response to that and, in particular, what the Ministry is doing to improve outcomes for consumers?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Further details would be set out in the Healthcare Services Bill, as we will put it up shortly.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, can I ask the Minister for his comments regarding the proposal in my Budget Debate speech to acknowledge allied health professionals' (AHPs') and pharmacists' expertise in a national subsidy framework for cost containment as well as to keep patients in the community, such as the extension of drug subsidy schemes to community pharmacies as well as extension of the CHAS scheme to allied health services in the community because we need a holistic approach to keep patients in the community?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the point about remuneration for public sector AHPs, a point that was raised by Ms Irene Quay, beyond salaries, MOH works with the clusters to enhance the value proposition of an AHP career in the public sector, and these are things that I mentioned by providing learning and development opportunities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I mentioned in my speech also about the skills framework for healthcare that was launched in 2019 that will cover various training opportunities and career plans that they can have.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As for pay, it is something that we will review.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We always want to make sure that it is competitive so that we can retain good AHPs in the public sector.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My question is directed at Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This is with respect to my cut on Greater MediSave Flexibility for senior citizens, particularly those above 60.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned in his reply that eight out of 10 patients pay less than $100 in cash as a result of their hospitalisation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just get a sense of the average amount that patients pay for the remaining 20% of that category?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In addition to that, what are the absolute numbers of hospitalisations we are talking about in that particular category, those who pay above $100?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I do not have those numbers to hand out, but if the Member could file a PQ, I would have those numbers to hand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since 2015, we have been significantly increasing aged care capacity in terms of nursing homes as well as community care, home and centre-based care facilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, the supply of home and daycare places has actually stabilised.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, in those areas where there is an imbalance, we are actually ramping up capacity in terms of new centres, as well as building new centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our focus now is on the quality and variety of aged care services available.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Earlier on in my speech, I said that we are actually looking at better integration of social and health services and, therefore, because the SACs have now come under MOH, together with the SCCs, we are now looking at a range of services that all these Senior Centres can offer within the community and, therefore, increasing access and availability of services for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: HPB collaborates, for instance, with the local retailers to offer price discounts for Healthier Choice symbol house brand products and we have been working closely with retailers, such as the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), Cold Storage and Sheng Siong.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will see what else we can do on this front.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But it is also worth pointing out that on healthier food, it does not cost so much to eat healthy.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: You can actually prepare chicken in healthier ways.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Is there a targeted timeframe for moving in a more broad-based way towards a VBH model in Singapore and will a roadmap be published towards that end?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This workgroup already comprised representatives from the various public healthcare institutions, so it is already quite broad-based.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we need to do it very carefully because, as the Member pointed out, we need a buy-in from both service providers as well as patients so that they are on this journey of value-driven care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to press on with this effort.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is already broad-based, involving most of our public healthcare institutions and they have a plan to gradually expand these conditions to more conditions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we would prefer to focus on these 17 for the time being to make sure that they are done well so that the same methodology, the same model, can then be replicated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If we rush into it, it may create more problems and difficulties.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we would prefer to focus on these 17, do it well and develop a dashboard so that we can get everybody on board and try to improve and optimise the care outcome and cost effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Later on, we can replicate it to other conditions.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Mr Chairman, as always, I would like to thank all Members for their active participation and for the very healthy debate and, of course, to Minister Gan Kim Yong, Senior Ministers of State Amy Khor, Lam Pin Min and Edwin Tong and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin and all the staff of MOH for the care they have given because you get explanations and the surgical precision of their responses.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
